messages:
Maya (Support): Customer emailed support — invoice shows ~2.4M tokens billed for last week but their dashboard 'served_tokens' shows ~1.9M. They say billing spike correlates with a batcher rollout. Can infra/billing look? Pasting their summary below.

Arun (Infra): pinging infra. Do we have any known prefetch/prefill behavior that could cause billed!=served? Could be continuous-batcher warmups or duplicate accounting when KV-prefetch and coalescing interact.

Ben (Billing): putting initial hypothesis: billing counts 'metered tokens' at ingress after batching/coalesce accounting; served_tokens is post-cache/dedup. If a prefetch or warmup path triggers metering before cache hit resolution, it could bill more. Need trace.

Maya (Support): Customer provided trace snippet and request IDs: req-0a1b2, req-0a1b3, req-0a1b9. They also ran a replay and saw meter spikes during background prefetch.

Arun (Infra): can you upload a quick example log lines? e.g. from runtime trace with fields: request_id, batch_id, metered_tokens, served_tokens, cache_hit.

Maya (Support): pasted (redacted):
```
[2026-02-18T09:12:14Z] req=0a1b2 batch=cb-34 metered_tokens=1200 served_tokens=0 cache_prefetch=true
[2026-02-18T09:12:14Z] req=0a1b2 batch=cb-34 served_tokens=1200 cache_hit=true
[2026-02-18T09:12:14Z] req=0a1b3 batch=cb-35 metered_tokens=800 served_tokens=0 prefetch=true
[2026-02-18T09:12:14Z] req=0a1b3 batch=cb-35 served_tokens=800 cache_hit=true
```

Jess (DevEx): interesting — logs show metering recorded on the prefetch attempt (metered_tokens nonzero) and then served_tokens later when cache hit returned. If metering runs at the start of the batch pipeline, background warmups could increment billed counters even if result ultimately served from cache.

Ben (Billing): that aligns with a gap we've seen. Current billing pipeline consumes metered events from ingress telemetry; it doesn't de-dupe by later cache_hit signals. We can change billing to prefer final attribution but need to evaluate correctness for other flows.

Arun (Infra): quick repro plan: enable continuous-batcher annotated logs on a small customer test, run workload with aggressive proactivity/prefetch, and compare: (1) ingress billed events, (2) final served events from post-cache. I can instrument a flag to emit correlation id across prefetch vs final.

Maya (Support): customer wants a timeline and whether we can apply manual credit if this was unintended for them. Please advise. Ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/INC-4123

Ben (Billing): provisional: if we confirm double-counting due to prefetch-only metering, we should offer one-time credit and schedule billing fix. Need repro and scope (how many customers affected).

Jess (DevEx): short-term mitigation: reduce aggressive prefetch for their org (rate-limit background prefetch) or toggle prefetch=false on their config. I'll prepare an opt-out patch we can flip.

Arun (Infra): doing instrumentation now. deploy-bot: launched experiment on staging with prefetch demotion flag.

deploy-bot: build/deploy 2026-02-18T09:28:00Z started for eng-infra/continuous-batcher-instrumentation (#421).

Maya (Support): thanks all — I'll update the customer with the mitigation (toggle prefetch) and ETA for follow-up after repro. Will attach logs they provided to the ticket. :thumbsup:

Ben (Billing): next steps: await repro results; if confirmed scope small -> credit; if widespread -> roll fix into metering pipeline.

Arun (Infra): note for postmortem: consider tagging metering events with final_attribution_id and delaying billing commit a short window for dedupe.

Jess (DevEx): filed follow-up RFC for prefetch attribution patterns, linking to ticket.

Maya (Support): closing interim loop with customer now, keeping ticket open until infra confirms.
